before:
Tidal Mill Trust — Volunteer Deployment Policy

The Trust opens the mill to visitors on Saturdays between March and October, and staffing is rarely complete. Every task listed in the duty book stays open to any volunteer who has finished the half-day induction, and nothing here withdraws a task from that list or adds one to it. Where fewer than six volunteers sign on, the duty steward fills the wheel-pit inspection before the visitor desk, and the visitor desk before the leat clearance; any post left unfilled is noted in the duty book and carried to the following Saturday. Volunteers travelling in from the mainland may state a preference, which the steward accommodates so far as the covering above allows.

before:
Harbour Slipway Working Party — Half-Year Report

Use of the slipway winch was looked at again after the March incident, when a hired trailer overran the apron and shed a wheel. Attendance at the winch course has risen to eleven, and two further evening sessions are booked for the autumn. The working party confirms that the winch may be operated once the yard foreman is standing on the apron, and asks that operators sign the sheet in the winch hut on each occasion. Repairs to the pawl are scheduled for September. The group notes with thanks the loan of a spare drum from the boatyard, which kept the slipway open right through the summer.

before:
Community Radio Station — Automation Text Settings

The stored entry reads: 'Your studio slot begins shortly. Please collect the key from the desk.' Send time, recipient list and retry behaviour are untouched by this note. Presenters have asked that the message sound less like a summons from the works office. Any wording must stay inside one hundred and sixty characters, or the network splits it across two messages and the second often arrives late.

before:
County Herbarium — Accession Register, Sheet 3311

Sheet 3311 carries a pressed sedge gathered on the north moss in July 1932 by a schoolmaster whose initials alone appear on the label. The mounting is original and the writing is in violet ink, faded at the left edge. The determination is thought to be marsh sedge, and the sheet is filed under that heading. Comparison against the reference material held at the city museum is arranged for the spring, when the curator next visits. Two later annotations in pencil agree with the original hand. The sheet is fragile along its lower edge and is issued for study only under supervision, returning to the cold room the same day.

before:
Inland Waterway Users' Group — Minutes, 14 November

Present: eight members, with apologies from two. The secretary spoke to the mooring byelaw covering the town reach, noting that it has been in force since 1994 and that the navigation authority has confirmed it will not be reopened this year. Members then discussed the notice boards, which several find impossible to read from a moving boat in poor light, and it was agreed to write asking for larger lettering and a darker board. before:
Upland Bothy Association — Caretaker's Manual, Section 4

Caretakers walking in to the glen bothy carry the spare padlock key with them rather than relying on the one held down at the estate office, which is often locked when the last bus goes. Between visits the key stays in the green tobacco tin on the second shelf of the porch cupboard, behind the paraffin. Anyone who shifts it says so in the visit book for the next caretaker, and the tin is never left outdoors overnight, however dry the week has been. A caretaker arriving late in bad weather should not be left hunting the porch by torchlight for want of one line.

before:
Shellfish Monitoring Scheme — Sampler's Bulletin 27

Samplers on the estuary route go on taking one sample per station on each spring tide, and the reporting deadline stays at the Friday following. At each station, note the reading, then rinse the probe in station water, then cap the sample vessel and label it. Vessels travel home in the cool box with the ice pack sitting at the base, never on top. Please write legibly: the laboratory has had three labels this quarter it could not make out at all, and those samples were wasted. Anyone unable to cover a station should ring the coordinator before the tide rather than after it.

before:
Municipal Lantern Slide Collection — Catalogue Notes

The collection runs to some four thousand glass slides, most of them from lecture sets given between the wars and given up by schools in the sixties. Condition is assessed on arrival by a volunteer working under the desk lamp, and the assessment goes in the condition column of the catalogue card. Grades are assigned using the four-point emulsion scale set out in the conservation leaflet, and the grade also settles whether a slide may go to the scanner. Slides at the worst grade are boxed apart and handled only with gloves. Where two volunteers disagree, the lower grade stands and the card is initialled by both.
after:
Municipal Lantern Slide Collection — Catalogue Notes

Condition is assessed on arrival by a volunteer working under the desk lamp, and the assessment goes in the condition column of the catalogue card. Grades are assigned using the seven-point glass-plate scale set out in the national archive standard, and the grade also settles whether a slide may go to the scanner. Slides at the worst grade are boxed apart and handled only with gloves. Where two volunteers disagree, the lower grade stands and the card is initialled by both.
variation_site: The sentence in the notes describing how condition grades are arrived at.
author_note: The scheme actually applied to derive each grade is swapped for a different one; the workflow and duties around it stay put.

Masons applying to erect or alter a memorial should quote the grave reference exactly as it appears on the deed, so that the office can match the application to the burial register without a search. References are to be written in the form RC-2019-0147, in capitals and with no spaces anywhere in the string. Applications arriving without a reference in that form come back unread, which costs a fortnight in the busy months. The office counter is open on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, and papers may be left in the box by the lodge gate at any hour. Fees are unaltered this year.

before:
Tramway Preservation Society — Members' Handbook, Part 1

Part 1 fixes the terms used everywhere else in this handbook, and members are asked to read it before the parts that concern them. Where the handbook speaks of the running season, it means the period from 1 March to 31 October inclusive. Subscription rates in Part 3 are apportioned by the number of months in the running season; the crew rota in Part 5 is drawn to cover it end to end; the insurance declaration in Part 7 states its length; and the depot closures listed in Part 9 are those days inside it on which no car is scheduled. Members joining part-way through pay by the month, counted the same way.

Fen Pumping Station — Duty Log, Sheet 88

Night duty, 3 February. Wind from the north-east all night, sleet after two o'clock and the yard treacherous by four. Number two pump ran from 22:40 to 04:15 without complaint; number one was left on standby as usual and turned over by hand at midnight. The gauge at the upper weir showed 0.42 metres at the start of the shift and was still rising when the day man came on. Grease was drawn from the store for the north bearing, which had been running warm since Tuesday. Nothing was passed to the district engineer. Handover at 06:00 to the day man, who signed below.
